correctness.rationale: Explicit invertible affine row/column reparametrization reduces every admissible operator to the ordered-pair line family. Discriminant-square root counting and affine-line intersections give a q-block Gram matrix. Fourier decomposition along slopes produces precisely two residual 2×2 blocks and the 2q sector; their exact characteristic polynomials give every stated multiplicity. Positivity of B± establishes that no additional kernel exists; B+=B−+qwwᵀ and the diagonal lower bound locate the sharp extremal eigenvalues. The standalone standard-library exact-integer checker independently reconstructs incidence matrices over F3,F5,F7,F9, checks exact power sums and annihilators, and verifies affine change-of-variable identities. The universal claim relies on the proof, not on those finite tests.

originality.rationale: The new asserted implication is the exact full singular spectrum, kernel and sharp positive-condition bound of the affine bilinear parameterized incidence operator; none of the inspected statements directly determines these for the constrained discriminant-square line subfamily with parameter repetitions. value.rationale: The bilinearly coupled two-parameter incidence family is a current object of spectral finite-field incidence analysis. Previous general results bound discrepancy but do not quantify exactly which parameter weights can be recovered. The theorem completes the entire nonconstant affine-coefficient sector: it gives a universal exact kernel (all and only parameter swaps), exact singular-value multiplicities, and a sharp best possible inverse-noise gain for every odd prime power. This closes a natural linear inverse problem, rather than computing one arbitrary small dimension or merely repeating the standard unweighted line-design norm.
